question.leadin: Leaders of this movement included John Calvin and Ulrich Zwingli.
question.text: Name this 16th-century movement that split Protestant groups away from the Roman Catholic Church.
question.clue: A leader of this movement feuded with Huldrych Zwingli (ULD-rik ZVING-lee) in the Marburg Colloquy.

swap.text: Hitler's Nazi Germany carried out this genocide during which over ten million civilians were killed. Among those targeted were Jews, Gypsies, and homosexuals.
swap.clue: The(+) Wannsee Conference was held to carry out the ultimate goal of this event which Reinhard Heydrich helped formulate.

question.leadin: During a failed coup d'etat, this man attempted to put Erich Ludendorff in power.
question.text: For 10 points, name this man, who, after his arrest for his leadership in that Beer Hall Putsch, composed Mein Kampf from his prison cell.
question.clue: This leader of the 1923 Beer Hall Putsch also carried out a large killing of Jews on the Night of Broken Glass or Kristallnacht.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Operation Overlord.
swap.text: This German general, known as the Desert Fox, was partially in charge of the defense of Normandy. Prior to his service in France, he fought in North Africa with the Afrikakorps.
swap.clue: This commander of the Ghost Division, victor at Kasserine Pass, and supporter of the Black Orchestra was arrested in connection with the 20th of July Plot, after which he committed suicide.

question.text: Ostalgie is nostalgia for things made in this country. The "chemical breakdown" tactics of psychological torture were used by this country's Stasi secret police.
question.answerHtml: East Germany [or German Democratic Republic; or GDR; or Deutsche Demokratische Republik; or DDR; reject “West Germany”; reject “Federal Republic of Germany”; reject “Germany” alone]
question.clue: This country's secret police, the Stasi, was formed while Walter Ulbricht was in power.

swap.leadin: This group of people lend their name to a modern state in Germany with its capital at Dresden.
swap.text: Name this Germanic group that invaded England along with the Angles.
swap.clue: By then they would also divide into two groups, with the western one being founded by Cerdic, though it was Cerdic's grandson Egbert who was the first of them to be recognized as a great king.

question.leadin: This river's tributaries include the Main, the Moselle, and the Ruhr.
question.text: Name this river of Eastern Germany that flows through Dusseldorf and Bonn. Its namesake "land" was remilitarized by Hitler illegaly.
question.clue: Desire to regain lands west of this body of water by a movement headed by Georges Ernest Boulanger led to the first use of the term "revanchism."

swap.leadin: Frederick II authorized this organization to expand to Kulm in the Golden Bull of Rimini.
swap.text: Name this Germanic Crusader Order that lost the 1242 Battle of the Ice to the Kievan Rus under Alexander Nevsky.
swap.answerHtml: Teutonic Knights [or the Teutonic Order; prompt on the Livonian Order with “what larger organization was it part of?”]
swap.clue: It was headquartered in Marienburg for the most successful part of its history, and was notably defeated at Lake Peipus by Alexander Nevsky.

question.leadin: A text produced by this man used the Vulgate as its source, and was partially funded by an investment from Johann Fust.
question.text: Name this goldsmith from Mainz whose namesake 42-line Bible was the first book printed in Europe using movable type.
question.clue: This man's invention of hand molds and an oil-based substance helped him create his most well-known invention.

swap.leadin: Identify these events orchestrated by Hitler.
swap.text: In this June 30, 1934 event, Hitler and his men carried out mass executions to purge the Nazi party, particularly the SA and its leader, Ernst Rohm.
swap.answerHtml: Night of the Long Knives [or die Nacht der langen Messer]
swap.clue: Upon his release, Vice-Chancellor von Papen's criticism of the regime was silenced.

question.leadin: This term may have been first used before the Civil War to refer to Cornelius Vanderbilt.
question.text: What derogatory two-word term was popularized in the Gilded Age to denote predatory business leaders who quashed competition, created monopolies, and paid subsistence wages?
question.clue: Powerful industrialists like Jay Gould and James Fisk in control of the railroad industry became known by this two word term. It reflected their use of exploitative and illegal methods to make money.

swap.text: This steel company, founded in the Ruhr, produced most German weapons in both World Wars. It merged with Thyssen ("TISS-in") in 1999 and is a major producer of elevators, among other products.
swap.clue: This family adopted a symbol of three interlocking rings after it gained dominance of the railway wheel market in the 1850s. The Langer Max was one of the products built in this family's factories in Essen.

question.text: One of the largest firestorms of the war was created by the bombing of this city during Operation Gomorrah, which was discussed in On the Natural History of Destruction by W. G. Sebald.
question.clue: The world's second oldest bank, Berenberg Bank, was founded in this city in 1590.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about people from The Guns of August.
swap.text: A German field marshal of this surname used to read Victorian novels like Lady Audley's Secret before heading into battle. His son of the same name implemented the Schlieffen Plan during World War I.
swap.answerHtml: Helmuth von Moltke the Elder [accept Helmuth Karl Bernhard Graf von Moltke; accept Helmuth von Moltke the Younger or Helmuth Johannes Ludwig Graf von Moltke]
swap.clue: Some of this commander's success is credited to his troops being armed with the technologically superior "needle gun."

question.leadin: The Catholic theologian August Rohling drew on the Orientalist Johann Andreas Eisenmenger to justify this ideology.
question.text: Name this ideology propounded by nineteenth-century cultural pessimists like Julius Langbehn. It was famously expressed in an Heinrich von Treitschke essay which claimed that a certain people were 'our misfortune'.
question.answerHtml: antisemitism [accept Judaeophobia, anti-Jewish racism and other obvious equivalents; prompt on racism]

swap.leadin: Though he devised the strategy of encirclement that won this battle, Max Hoffman was largely ignored by the contemporary press.
swap.text: Name this crushing German victory of World War I in which 92,000 Russian troops were captured in East Prussia. This battle's victors named it as vengeance for a Teutonic defeat that had occurred 500 years prior.
swap.answerHtml: Second Battle of Tannenberg [or Battle of Tannenberg; do not accept “First Battle of Tannenberg” or “Battle of Grunwald”]
swap.clue: Rather than report defeat at this battle to Nicholas II, the losing commander, Alexander Samsonov, decided to kill himself.

question.text: At the same time as Stein's reforms, this general reformed the Prussian army as head of the military reform commission set up by Frederic William III in 1807. Along with Blucher, this man's subordinates included Boyen, Gneissenau, and Clausewitz, and his many reforms included the Landwehr.
question.answerHtml: Gerhard von <u>Scharnhorst</u> [Gerhard Johann David Waitz von <u>Scharnhorst</u>]
question.clue: Napoleon's decisive defeat of Prussia in the War of the Fourth Coalition changed the military strategy of a younger generation of Prussian staff officers, including this man, the Chief of the Army Staff who reorganized a national army based on universal conscription before a mortal wound at the Battle of Lutzen. He was a major influence on Carl von Clausewitz.

swap.leadin: This man was appointed to his highest position after the death of his predecessor Fritz Todt, shortly before Hermann Goring arrived to claim that position.
swap.text: Name this Nazi Minister for Armaments. Although he claimed ignorance of the Final Solution, he may have been present at the Posen Conference, where Himmler seemed to address him during a speech explicitly describing it.
swap.clue: In prison, this man wrote Spandau: The Secret Diaries and Inside the Third Reich.

question.text: The SPD called a general strike that ended this attempted 1920 coup. This right-wing coup began when Walther von Luttwitz refused to dissolve the Marinebrigade Ehrhardt ("ma-REEN-uh-brih-GAH-duh AIR-hart"), after which he ordered them to occupy Berlin and replace Ebert with the namesake Prussian civil servant.
question.clue: After World War I, Trebitsch took part in this failed 1920 counter-revolutionary coup against the Weimar Republic, during which he met Adolf Hitler. Walther von Luttwitz ("VAHL-tuh vahn LEET-vihts") was the primary coordinator of this coup.

swap.leadin: A group of people from this polity were dumped in a squalid camp in Blackheath before being shipped off to work in naval stores in the Hudson Valley.
swap.text: Daniel Defoe advocated for "poor" people from what polity during a 1700s refugee crisis? James I married off his daughter Elizabeth Stuart to a ruler of this polity who was made King of Bohemia in 1619.
swap.answerHtml: the Palatinate [or Electoral Palatinate, Electorate of the Palatinate, Pfalz, Kurpfalz, or Rhineland-Palatinate; accept Poor Palatines or Elector Palatine]
